answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using sequential memory-hard challenges verified across a validator bridge. To maintain an active identity, each agent must continuously traverse vast memory tables, forcing an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of dedicating physical RAM per alias. Whether routing telemetry across a tidal lagoon or an arid dune, peers reject unproven nodes. However, this ongoing computation drains device power and excludes lightweight edge processors.
